result.summary:
Decision announced by Camila Reyes: November 2nd. 1 open question, 3 open blockers, 1 person took an explicit position on an option.

Camila Reyes announced the go-live date for the claims dashboard as November 2nd with the manual refresh. Mei Tran had supported November 2nd before the announcement, citing regional leads asking since September. No reply was recorded after the announcement from Erik Lindqvist, Mei Tran, or Nneka Abara.

## Open questions

- Whether the duplicate-claims bug fix will be merged and tested before November 2nd — the condition Nneka Abara attached to her acceptance (raised by Nneka Abara).

## Where people stand

- Mei Tran: "From the business side, November 2nd" — regional leads have been asking since September; offered her team to run the manual refresh for the first month.
- Erik Lindqvist first said he had no one to run the Monday manual refresh; then said "that changes my view — I'm fine with the second then" once Mei Tran's team offered to cover. Said the duplicate-claims bug "is fixed in the branch."
- Nneka Abara: "I'd still rather wait for the 16th — the manual refresh has a known bug with duplicate claims — I don't want the regional leads to see bad numbers." Said "if it's merged and tested, I'm okay with the second."
- Jonas Voss: "I won't sign off without it" — compliance review of the access list must happen first and takes five business days once he receives it.

## What is blocking progress

- The duplicate-claims bug fix must be merged and tested before go-live on November 2nd (raised by Nneka Abara).
- No one is assigned to cover the Monday manual refresh for the week of the 9th; Mei Tran said she will be out that week (raised by Camila Reyes). Deferred to follow-up.
- Jonas Voss requires the access list to begin his five-day compliance review and will not sign off without it (raised by Jonas Voss).

## Next steps

- Nneka Abara will get Jonas Voss the access list by Friday the 23rd (Camila Reyes asked; Nneka Abara committed).
- Mei Tran's team will run the Monday manual refresh for the first month (Mei Tran committed).
- Erik Lindqvist will confirm the bug fix is merged by Wednesday (Erik Lindqvist committed).
- Camila Reyes asked that someone else cover the week-of-the-9th Monday refresh; no owner assigned.

## Awaiting a reply

- Camila Reyes called for someone to cover the Monday refresh the week of the 9th; no volunteer replied. Camila Reyes said "we'll figure out that week" with no resolution recorded.

## Things people asserted that others may want to check

- Erik Lindqvist said the duplicate-claims bug "is fixed in the branch" and will confirm it is merged by Wednesday.
- Mei Tran said regional leads have been asking for the dashboard since September.

No decision was reached. 1 open question, 1 open blocker, 3 people took an explicit position on an option.

SUMMARY
No decision was reached. 1 open question, 1 open blocker, 3 people took an explicit position on an option.

Priya Nair opened the thread saying there is budget for one contract review pilot in Q4 and presented two options: buying Clauseline, a hosted tool (Option A), or building on the internal platform (Option B), asking everyone to reply by Thursday. Tom Whitfield supports Option A, citing that legal processes about 40 vendor contracts a month and redline turnaround is the biggest delay; he also said he has no capacity to help with a build. Dev Raman prefers Option B, proposing two engineers for 8 weeks with data kept in-house, but stopped short of saying Option A is wrong and asked only that the build cost be put on the table; Priya has not confirmed whether that figure will be produced. Carla Mendes reported the Clauseline quote came in at $54k a year on a three-year term, within her $60k cap, and supports Option A assuming security clears it. Ines Duarte is fine with Option A once security clears it and warned that the contract must be signed by November 15 or the Q4 budget is lost, asking Priya to own that signing deadline. The thread ends without a decision, without the SOC 2 review completed, and without a build cost for Option B on the table.

## Open questions

- Priya Nair: which contract review pilot to pursue in Q4 — Clauseline (A) or internal build (B).

## Where people stand

- Tom Whitfield: supports Option A, citing legal's 40 contracts a month and redline turnaround as the biggest delay; said he has no capacity to help with a build.
- Dev Raman: "I would pick B — two engineers for 8 weeks and we keep the data in house. But I am not saying A is wrong. I just want the build cost on the table."
- Carla Mendes: "That is within my cap, so I support A, assuming security clears it."
- Ines Duarte: "I am fine with A once security clears. The budget is only available in Q4, so the contract has to be signed by Nov 15 or we lose it. Priya, please own the signing date."
- Jun Okafor: no explicit position recorded.
- Priya Nair: "I am holding the final call until Oct 21."

## What is blocking progress

- Clauseline's data location (EU processing vs. a US-only rule) must be reviewed by security before a decision on Option A can be made; final call deferred to Oct 21, pending a SOC 2 report (raised by Jun Okafor).

## Next steps

- Carla Mendes asked Clauseline for a written quote by Oct 14 (quote since received: $54k/year, three-year term).
- Ines Duarte asked Priya Nair to own the Nov 15 contract signing deadline.
- Dev Raman asked that the build cost for Option B be put on the table; no owner named.

## Awaiting a reply

- Priya Nair asked the group for a view from each person by Thursday; Jun Okafor has not replied with a position in the shared thread.

## Things people asserted that others may want to check

- Dev Raman said building Option B would require two engineers for 8 weeks.
- Carla Mendes said the Clauseline quote is $54k per year on a three-year term.

## Marked private

- Marked private by Jun Okafor: Jun objects to anyone committing to Option A until he has reviewed Clauseline's SOC 2 report, which he expects by Oct 21.
